A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, algorithms, proofs, experiments, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G report original simulation experiments and FUDOKI text-to-image sampling results on GenEval.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain original empirical results and add higher-order sampler comparisons and a numerical integration grid sensitivity experiment.

M1.justification: The time-corrected and location-corrected procedures, training objective, and Algorithms 1–8 are retained, including the existing extensions to general conditional rates and few-step sampling. Added intuitive explanations and grid-size experiments do not change the proposed methods.

E1.justification: Both versions cover blockwise AR(1) simulations with dimensions 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15, uniform and masked sources, and FUDOKI/GenEval image generation. The nine-dimensional example highlighted in v2's main text was already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: v2 adds RK2 and RK2-Trapezoid from Ren et al. (2025b) to both simulation and GenEval comparisons. Figures 2, 3, 5, and 6 and Table 2 therefore substantially broaden the evaluated comparators beyond v1's tau-leaping/Euler baselines.

E3.justification: The simulation step grid adds K = 40, 75, and 100 to the previous grid ending at 50. New Table 4 varies integration grid size m from 4 to 128 at fixed K = 8. Existing training budgets, sample counts, and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted sensitivity study of the time-corrected sampler's numerical integration grid in Table 4, examining generation quality and sampling time. The existing location-correction threshold study in Table 3 is unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten runs per simulation setting and display simulation error bars. GenEval tables remain point estimates, with no added seed information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 revises and extends the simulation curves, adds eight higher-order baseline rows to Table 2, and introduces the grid-sensitivity results in Table 4. For example, Table 4 reports GenEval scores of 72.557 at m = 16 and 68.661 at m = 128, both with K = 8. All twelve original Table 2 rows and all eight Table 3 rows are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds an explicit Euler-sampler proof sketch for Theorem 1. v2 also corrects the extra factor 2 multiplying the squared schedule derivative in Lemma 3's proof. The main theorem statements, assumptions, and complexity guarantees remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Contribution 2 narrows its stated complexity comparison from 'other parallel samplers' to tau-leaping and Euler samplers. The abstract and conclusion otherwise retain the central claims about corrected sampling, error bounds, and efficiency.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly connects the masked-source advantage over higher-order baselines to posterior time-independence, while describing performance against RK2-Trapezoid under uniform sources as competitive. Appendix H.2 also introduces the practical qualification that increasing integration resolution need not improve generation quality.

D1.justification: Appendix H.1 newly states that experiments use four NVIDIA A100 GPUs. This is additional hardware disclosure, not evidence of a hardware change. Existing model architectures, training hyperparameters, default integration settings, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work survey are retained. Sections 6 and H add more specific empirical positioning against Ren et al. (2025b)'s deterministic higher-order solvers, distinguishing masked-source advantages from competitiveness under uniform sources.

P1.justification: v2 adds short intuitive explanations after Equations 9 and 11, expands experimental discussion, moves notation into Appendix A, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Author and affiliation text also changes, but the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references adopt a two-column conference layout. Experimental plots are redrawn with expanded legends and ranges, simulation examples are redistributed between main text and appendix, Table 2 expands, and Table 4 is added. Reflow also makes previously clipped proof equations fully visible.

improvement.justification: The higher-order comparisons and grid-resolution study strengthen the evidence for when the samplers are useful beyond v1's first-order comparisons. The Euler proof sketch, corrected Lemma 3 calculation, and improved equation display also increase completeness and clarity. These provide a limited overall strengthening of the existing paper, whose central methods and theoretical guarantees are retained.
